title: Ghost-chunk reconciliation and epoched session fix for hosted SSE disconnects
creator: Asha Raman
description: Multiple customers reported sessions that, after a mid-stream tcp disconnect and successful reconnect, produced duplicated or truncated token sequences and occasional 'ghost' chunks (server-generated partial chunks that were never marked as acknowledged). Investigation shows a race between checkpoint GC and multiplexed client reconnects which allowed stale buffer segments to be merged into new streams. This ticket stabilizes hosted SSE behavior by introducing session epoching, idempotent chunk identifiers, and a server-side drain/validation step on reconnect.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running streaming request from a client that receives tokens as chunks via SSE
2) Force a network disconnect mid-stream (simulate NAT timeout or client suspend)
3) Reconnect quickly and resume the session using existing session token/stream id
4) Observe duplicated tokens, truncated final messages, or ghost chunks appearing after reconnection
5) Reproduces intermittently under concurrency and with aggressive GC settings on the host-side buffer manager
investigation_summary: Root cause: server-side session checkpoint GC could purge in-memory stream fragments while a reconnect handshake was still completing. Because chunk IDs were scoped only to stream start time (not epoched), a reconnection could reuse an id range and cause the reassembly pipeline to splice old, partially-purged chunks into the resumed output. Secondary factor: multiplexed connections for the same session allowed out-of-order ACKs to mark stale data as valid. We reproduced locally with a test harness that fast-forwards GC timers and simulates concurrent reconnects.
temporary_mitigation: Applied a short-term config change to increase session checkpoint TTL from 30s to 180s for affected clusters and added a per-connection backoff recommendation in the customer-facing KB. This reduced incidents while we implemented the long-term fix.
implementation_notes: 1) Add session epoch number on session state and handshake. Epoch increments on any full reconnect handshake that presents prior session ID.
implementation_notes_2: 2) Generate globally-unique chunk IDs including session-epoch to make chunk application idempotent.
implementation_notes_3: 3) On reconnect, server performs a drain-and-validate step: compute expected next-chunk-id for epoch and reject/hold any chunks that don't match until client replays from expected offset.
implementation_notes_4: 4) Add test harness scenarios covering concurrent reconnects, fast GC, and multiplexed clients. Add unit tests for idempotent chunk application and e2e test in staging that asserts no duplicates under failure injection.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate or truncated tokens observed in staged e2e harness under reconnect-failure-injection (0/1000 runs)
Session checkpoint TTL remains configurable but default behavior removes need for expanded TTL in prod
No regressions in latency under normal load (measured 99th percentile token latency within 5% of baseline)
New metrics exposed: session_epoch_count, chunk_reject_rate, reconnect_drain_duration
rollout_plan: Feature branch and PR with unit tests (target merge to main)
Canary deploy to two low-traffic clusters with feature flag off by default
Enable feature flag for 5% of traffic for 24 hours, monitor chunk_reject_rate and duplicate_token alerts
If stable, ramp to 30% then 100% over 48 hours
If regressions, rollback by disabling feature flag and revert PR if needed
customer_reports: Customer-A: high-volume chat app observed duplicate messages in 23 sessions over 24h
Customer-B: occasional truncated final paragraphs leading to support escalations
rollback_plan: If consumer-facing regressions occur after canary, instantly toggle feature-flag off. If issue persists, perform emergency revert of PR and re-enable extended checkpoint TTL as interim. Communicate with impacted customers via account owners.
postmortem_actions: Ship migration: run one-off job to reconcile any sessions in ambiguous state (script included)
Add alert that detects session_epoch_gaps > 0.5% per hour
Document recommended client-side reconnect backoffs in SDKs
